summary: ORVEX is a story-driven educational game that teaches how interconnected engineering decisions shape the outcome of a space mission. Players progress from junior astronaut training to planning, engineering, commanding, and operating a lunar research outpost. Unlike quiz-based learning, choices made early — payload, power, budget, crew — persist and reshape later scenarios; a Decision Trace and Mission Debrief then explain why a result occurred and what alternatives existed. The project targets a proposed learning gap: beginners often understand subsystems (payload, propulsion, power, life support) in isolation but not their trade-offs and coupling. ORVEX is grounded in public NASA references and uses a transparent, simplified simulation with clearly labeled assumptions. The report presents the concept, research process, scientific basis, technical approach, and a feasible hackathon MVP: one connected design → consequence → debrief loop.
